thread:
maria: Hey team, customer on Vercel Edge is seeing intermittent 401s when the browser hits our Edge TS SDK endpoint. Happens only from prod build, not in local dev.

maria: Repro flow: browser -> /api/proxy (Vercel Edge fn) -> Redwood hosted API. Upstream logs show 'missing Authorization header' even though client included it.

maria: Quick snippets:
```js
// client -> same-origin call to our Vercel edge route
await fetch('/api/proxy', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${userToken}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
})

// Vercel Edge function (simplified)
export default async (req) => {
  const auth = req.headers.get('authorization') || req.headers.get('Authorization')
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: auth, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: await req.text()
  })
  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status })
}
```

maria: package.json excerpts: client uses @redwood/edge-sdk@0.9.1, edge lambda is built with @redwood/edge-sdk@0.10.0 (weirdly).

sam: thanks — can you paste the exact upstream request headers (from our API logs) and edge fn logs? also which region?

maria: logs: upstream received request with headers:
```
accept: application/json
content-type: application/json
host: api.redwood.example
user-agent: redwood/edge-client
# NO authorization header present
```
Edge fn log around same time:
```
Edge request headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'authorization': 'Bearer abc...'}
Forwarding Authorization -> present
fetch to api.redwood.example returned 401
```

maria: so the edge fn saw the header but the upstream didn't. intermittent (not every request).

sam: hmm. two possibilities: 1) Vercel edge fetch wrapper or runtime is stripping Authorization on outbound cross-origin fetch when preflight fails, 2) header case normalization / duplicate header bug between SDK versions.

sam: can you repro with curl from an edge-like env (i.e., run the edge function locally with vercel dev or with wrangler for CF) and capture?

maria: repro with curl from our CI (which uses node18) to the edge fn: it always forwards auth -> upstream OK. Only browser -> edge fn -> upstream path shows the 401.

devon: flag: a recent SDK change in 0.10.0 normalized header accessors in the edge runtime (we switched internal helper from req.headers.get('Authorization') to req.headers.get('authorization') to match Cloudflare). That shouldn't drop headers but could interact with Vite/Vercel dev/build differences.

devon: also, Vercel edge runtime will sometimes coalesce headers for performance; I remember a bug where fetch() calls with an empty body + forwarded headers could trigger a preflight path flip and the browser would do an OPTIONS preflight to /api/proxy (same-origin) and then the edge fn's runtime would treat the subsequent POST differently.

maria: note: prod build uses Vite + terser; dev is raw vite dev server. Customer only on prod build on Vercel.

ben: two quick triage things: 1) confirm if client is sending the Authorization as a CORS-safelisted header or not (Authorization is not safelisted, so browser sends preflight). 2) ensure /api/proxy returns the right CORS preflight headers (Access-Control-Allow-Headers should include Authorization). If preflight fails, browser may omit Authorization on POST.

maria: we checked /api/proxy response to OPTIONS: it returns Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, X-Requested-With — does NOT include Authorization. ah.

maria: adding Authorization to Access-Control-Allow-Headers in the edge function stops the 401s locally (we tested).

sam: confirm for customer? that's likely the root cause then: browser preflight for Authorization was rejected so the actual POST did not include the header. Intermittency could be from some requests routed by proxies that cached the old preflight response or served without updated headers.

devon: long-term fix: SDK should document and surface a warning when used from browser -> edge fn -> hosted api flow, telling users to set CORS allow-headers or to store API key on serverless env and use server-side credentials instead of forwarding user token for that path. Also we should ensure the edge runtime preserves header casing/normalization across versions.

ben: short-term customer workaround: set API key on Vercel Edge function as REDWOOD_API_KEY and call hosted API directly from edge fn (avoid forwarding Authorization from browser). That reduces surface area and avoids preflight for the browser call (same-origin set-cookie etc).

maria: applied workaround for customer and they confirm the 401s stopped. raising this to P2 since it's a config doc gap and a small SDK UX improvement.

devon: I'll open an internal issue to: 1) add a note in edge SDK README about preflight/Authorization, 2) add a runtime compatibility test between 0.9.x and 0.10.x header behavior, 3) consider a warning in the SDK when detect edge usage without CORS allow headers.

ben: released patch 0.10.1 to npm that exposes a helper `getHeader(req, 'authorization')` that works across runtimes; also added docs.

deploy-bot: rolled out @redwood/edge-sdk@0.10.1 to hosted CDN at 2026-09-12T18:23:00Z (canary then stable).

maria: thx all — customer fixed with env-key workaround, will follow up to get them to upgrade to 0.10.1 and/or add proper Access-Control-Allow-Headers in their edge handler.

sam: marking thread resolved-for-now; reopen if they see regressions. :thumbsup:
